Golden Cauliflower with Lemon Tahini

A simple and rewarding way to roast cauliflower. The tahini dressing adds richness, and a little parsley brings freshness. Serve it alongside your favorite grains or legumes.

Estimated total
35–40 min (subject to oven and floret size)
Method
Oven
Ingredients & Method ↓

Development edition · Awaits kitchen testing.

Ingredients Method Storage

Ingredients

How many people?
2

FOR A LARGER BATCH

Use multiple baking sheets or roast in batches to avoid crowding. The sauce water should still be added gradually as needed.

Estimated to serve 2 people as a generous side.

  • 600 g cauliflower florets
  • 1.5 tbsp olive oil
  • ½ tsp ground cumin
  • Salt and black pepper, to taste
  • 2 tbsp tahini
    Missing this?

    Use thick plain yogurt · 3 tbsp

    It becomes fresher and tangy without the sesame flavor. Start with less lemon juice and adjust to taste. Skip adding water unless needed to thin it out. (Contains dairy).

  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • Water, as needed
  • Chopped parsley, to serve (optional)

Contains sesame.

Method

You'll need
Baking sheet · Mixing bowl · Whisk

Roast

01

Prepare the cauliflower

Heat the oven to 220°C / 425°F. Dry the cauliflower florets well if they are wet. In a large bowl, toss the cauliflower florets with the olive oil, ground cumin, Salt and black pepper, to taste until evenly coated.

02

Arrange on a baking sheet

Spread the florets on a baking sheet in a single layer without crowding them. Place the cut surfaces flat against the pan where possible.

03

Roast until golden

Roast in the oven, starting to check around the 25-minute mark. Turn the pieces as needed and continue roasting until they are deeply golden and tender.

Look for: Golden edges and stems that yield to the tip of a knife.

Finish

04

Make the tahini sauce

In a small bowl, whisk together the tahini and lemon juice. The mixture will seize and thicken at first. Add Water, as needed a splash at a time, whisking continuously, until the sauce is creamy and easily drizzled.

Extra tip

Add the water slowly. It takes a moment for the tahini to absorb the water and smooth out.

05

Serve

Transfer the roasted cauliflower to a plate, drizzle with the tahini sauce, and top with Chopped parsley, to serve (optional) if using.

IF YOURS LOOKS...

If the sauce looks split or overly thick after adding lemon, keep adding water a teaspoon at a time and whisk vigorously until smooth.

Serve with

Serve as a generous side dish.

Storage & Prep ahead

Cauliflower is best served fresh from the oven to keep its texture.

Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. The sauce can be stored separately.
